clue.text: Top seat alongside head of trade

definitions.note: verb: to top is to beat or outdo

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of trade is used

parts.note: seat is a polite word for the backside, the rump

explanation.surface: A seat is found beside the person heading a trade body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alongside' simply places the backside synonym next to the T.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat or outdo someone's card or effort is to top it, as a higher suit does.

clue.text: Somewhere in church, patterns all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Patterns in a church are chaotic.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross arm of a church building, running across the nave.

clue.text: Open champion finally embraced by team from America?

indicators.note: embraced by means the final letter sits inside the country's letters

parts.note: US is the United States

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of champion

parts.note: a crew is a rowing team

explanation.surface: A golf Open winner hugged by a US team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open champion' suggests golf, but Open is the definition as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a lid or cap by twisting it is to open it.

clue.text: Servant in part of novel?

explanation.surface: A servant appearing in a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A young attendant or messenger, and one side of a sheet in a book.

clue.text: Total wrong — on the contrary!

parts.note: a guess that is out is wrong, as in 'your sums are out'
the contrary of wrong is correct, so this phrase gives the opposite of the previous word

explanation.surface: Someone says a sum is totally wrong, then claims the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the contrary' looks like a throwaway rejoinder but supplies the opposite of 'wrong'.
explanation.definitionFit: An outright victory is complete or total, with nothing held back.

clue.text: Pure tuna mixed with a condiment

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are combined and reordered

explanation.surface: Pure tuna stirred together with a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Untainted, free of pollution or impurities.

clue.text: Fascinated, talked out loud

indicators.note: out loud signals that the word is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: rapped means talked, as in rapping chat

explanation.surface: Someone captivated and speaking aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely absorbed or spellbound.

clue.text: Troughs, say, in middle of pigsty

indicators.note: in places the speaking word inside the two central letters
middle of takes the central pair of letters of pigsty

parts.note: to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Feeding troughs in the centre of a pigsty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Channels for carrying away water are long open troughs.

clue.text: Time to join friend for match

parts.note: an ally is a supporter or friend

explanation.surface: Time for a friend to come to a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a game but is the verb to correspond.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that agree or correspond are said to coincide.

clue.text: Whiff of Melbourne, perhaps, with English cake

parts.note: Melbourne is a city of the Australian state of Victoria, so this is the possessive 'Victoria's'
pong is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A smell from Melbourne alongside an English cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Melbourne as one example of a place in that state. The answer is a British jam-and-cream sponge named after the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic British layered sponge filled with jam and cream.

clue.text: Old weapon as good in the main, imperfect originally

indicators.note: the letter for good sits inside the word for the main

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of imperfect

explanation.surface: An old weapon, decent enough at sea but flawed from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A light iron-tipped spear used by southern African peoples, historically a weapon of war.

clue.text: Excellent money

definitions.meaning: funds used to start or run a business

explanation.surface: Someone delighted at being paid well.
explanation.definitionFit: One word serves both as old-fashioned praise and as invested wealth or funds.

clue.text: Sovereign is backing father

definitions.note: verb or noun: to father, or a male parent animal

indicators.note: backing means the pair of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A monarch supports a father figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A sire is a male parent, especially of a horse, and to sire is to beget.

clue.text: Tolerate resistance

definitions.meaning: to put up with, as in 'I can't bear it'

explanation.surface: Putting up with opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with something, and a determined act of opposition, share this word.

clue.text: Extremely precise

explanation.surface: Something exceptionally exact.
explanation.definitionFit: An intensifier meaning highly, and an adjective meaning exact or actual, as in 'that same moment'.

clue.text: Lolly, something to eat

explanation.surface: A sweet treat to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lolly' suggests a lollipop but is British slang for money; the answer is slang for cash too.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a slang term for cash and the staple baked loaf.

clue.text: Waste material rotten, bitter mostly

parts.note: food gone off is rotten

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the beer is dropped

parts.note: bitter is a British type of ale

explanation.surface: Rubbish that is rotten and mostly bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the 'off-fall', offcuts of a carcass, and by extension refuse or waste.

clue.text: Early meeting might go to pieces quickly

parts.note: noun: strength or force
to shatter or fall apart
rapidly, at speed

explanation.surface: A dawn meeting could easily fall apart in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' looks like a verb but is the noun for strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A business discussion held over the first meal of the day, before work starts.

clue.text: Perfect — unlike a cricket ball?

definitions.meaning: a cricket ball has a raised stitched join round it

explanation.surface: Something flawless, compared with a cricket ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth and flawless, and literally having no stitched join.

clue.text: To the best of my understanding, it's the horizon on a clear day?

definitions.text: To the best of my understanding
definitions.meaning: a hedging phrase meaning 'as I see it'

definitions.text: it's the horizon on a clear day?
definitions.meaning: read literally, the horizon is the furthest point one's eyes reach

explanation.surface: A hesitant opinion followed by a remark on a long view.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for limited knowledge, read literally, describes the limit of one's eyesight.

clue.text: Winger down

explanation.surface: A wing player who has been brought down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer but is a bird; 'down' is the verb to gulp.
explanation.definitionFit: A forked-tailed migrant bird, and the verb to gulp food or drink.

clue.text: Woven carpets in bands of various colours

indicators.note: woven means the letters are interlaced into a new order

explanation.surface: Carpets woven with colourful stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranges of colours, as when light is split by a prism into a rainbow.

clue.text: King ending in Bangladesh, an Asian ruler

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A king's reign finishes in Bangladesh.
explanation.definitionFit: A title for a ruler or official in Central Asia, as in Genghis.

clue.text: Bake unusual British dish on a skewer

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Cooking an odd British dish on a skewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of meat grilled on a spit or skewer.

clue.text: Argument about river fish

indicators.note: about means the quarrel word goes round the river letter

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A dispute over fish in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A small herring-like sea fish of European waters.

clue.text: Hairstyle attributed to supermodel

indicators.note: the style is credited to the word supermodel because it sits within its letters

explanation.surface: A haircut credited to a famous model.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent wave is a chemically set curly style.

clue.text: Old fogey seen in two parties

indicators.note: two means the party word is written twice over

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A stuffy old person spotted at two parties.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct flightless bird, by extension someone old-fashioned.

clue.text: Arm possibly lacerated initially, one needing doctor

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of lacerated

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A cut arm needing a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm is one example of a body's projecting members.

clue.text: In blessing, everything is swell

indicators.note: In places the word for everything inside the word for a blessing

parts.note: a boon is a favour or benefit
all means the whole lot

explanation.surface: When things are blessed, all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like the slang adjective for great but is the verb to expand.
explanation.definitionFit: To expand or puff up, as a sail does in wind.

clue.text: Name ultimately I spelt wrong in letter

indicators.note: ultimately points to the closing letter of Name
wrong means these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone admits misspelling a name in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges I and SPELT into PISTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal letter, as in the New Testament books written by apostles.

clue.text: Shock — what cricketer may do?

definitions.meaning: a bowler knocks the batsman's wicket down

explanation.surface: A startling moment in a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone, and literally to knock a batsman over with a delivery.

clue.text: Part of the orchestra in the money?

definitions.meaning: the section of trumpets, trombones and horns

explanation.surface: Musicians in an orchestra who are well paid.
explanation.definitionFit: The trumpet and trombone section, and a British informal term for cash.
